answer.location_description: Small off-centre patch on the right side of the image, just below the middle (about rows 15-17, columns 19-22). This is lung or periphery about 10-15 mm to the right of the nodule centre, not the nodule itself.
answer.shortcut_type: localized bright patch/marker at fixed off-centre location
answer.mechanism: Hidden unit 9 (bias +88, so it is always active) has a compact block of large positive weights at rows 15-17, columns 19-22, so brightness there raises its activation. Unit 9's net effect through layer 2 points toward malignant. Its main malignant routes are its negative weights to layer-2 units u1, u5, u7 and u9, each of which carries a negative output weight. These outweigh its push into u0 and u10. Several other layer-1 units (1, 2, 3, 4, 15, 18, 21) also lean positive in the same few pixels, which adds a weaker push the same way.
answer.evidence: Unit 9 rows 15-17, columns 19-22 read 73 81 62 47 / -44 44 78 67 / 79 81 71 63. That is 11 of 12 weights at 44 or above in a unit whose other weights look like noise of about ±80, which is unlikely by chance anywhere in the network. Nearby weights are also high: row 15 columns 16 and 18 are 79 and 80, and row 16 columns 21-23 are 78 67 71. Tracing unit 9 through layer 2 to the output gives a net positive (malignant) contribution of roughly +7000 in products of integer weights. At pixels (16,21) and (17,21), about 22 of the 32 hidden units have positive weights, many of them large, for example 85, 71, 69 and 68. This cross-unit support is weaker and only suggestive. The bias toward this spot is not overwhelming, so confidence is moderate.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly detects bright, dense tissue in the central region where the nodule sits. Units 18 and 20 have strongly positive weights in about rows 10-17, columns 6-17, and units 1, 8 and 27 respond to broad brightness. All of these drive the logit toward malignant, so larger and denser central nodules read as malignant.
